changed_existing_paragraphs.before: Inferring gear microgeometry from transmission error requires distinguishing contact sensitivity from geometrical recovery. For a quasistatic operator with fixed geometry and compliance, we prove that nonnegative dedendum relief outside loaded support is exactly invisible, and extend the result to coupled linear elastic contact. An implicit contact tangent connects invariance with local sensitivities and the resolution of a discretized relief field. Profile likelihood and Monte Carlo experiments separate exact invariance from weak practical identifiability: for the nominal pair, median scaled dedendum error falls from 0.394 to 0.106 when the relief start moves deeper into contact, using 100 realizations, 120 observations, 300 Nm and 0.1 µm Gaussian noise. Equal-budget controls reveal angular-sampling effects and no statistically resolved benefit of the tested two-load allocation. Same-operator restricted fits across four compliance formulations preserve the distinction between marginal and deeper support. A finite-element contact comparison isolates a dedendum response of 0.179 µm RMS, close to the analytical 0.197 µm, yet an addendum-only inverse attains the same residual and dedendum profiles remain flat. An eight-phase material-removal control gives 0.4–2.1 nm centred changes outside contact, delimiting exact invariance to fixed compliance. None of four formulations meets the adopted 5% research target on twelve external amplitude references. These results yield a pre-inversion support diagnostic and operator-conditioned limits on observability without establishing physical profile recovery.

changed_existing_paragraphs.before: Limitations and outlook. All inversions use synthetic data, and the external reference is a published set of finite-element amplitudes rather than measured waveforms from gears with known modifications. The analytical operator reduces each candidate pair to one effective normal contact, and the finite-element generator is two-dimensional plane-strain; both are frictionless and quasistatic. The gap-only inverse operators retain fixed sections, normals and contact coordinates; the separate material-removal control relaxes the fixed-section assumption by reassembling elasticity. Dynamic effects, mounting deviations [17], wide-face effects [16] and the manufactured root fillet are outside this reduction. The finite-element gap tests share the nominal sections with the analytical model, and the omitted engagement-transition phases may carry information that cannot be counted until their contact is resolved. Profile-likelihood thresholds are nominal diagnostics because discrepancy is deterministic. Future work should (i) apply the support diagnostic to measured transmission error from gears with certified relief, (ii) resolve engagement transitions and fillet contact in the forward model, and (iii) replace the assumed noise scale and nominal likelihood thresholds by a calibrated discrepancy model within a Bayesian framework [40,41].
changed_existing_paragraphs.after: Limitations and outlook. All inversions use synthetic data, and the external reference is a published set of finite-element amplitudes rather than measured waveforms from gears with known modifications. The analytical operator reduces each candidate pair to one effective normal contact, and the finite-element generator is two-dimensional plane-strain; both are frictionless and quasistatic. The gap-only inverse operators retain fixed sections, normals and contact coordinates; the separate material-removal control relaxes the fixed-section assumption by reassembling elasticity. Dynamic effects, mounting deviations [17], wide-face effects [16] and the manufactured root fillet are outside this reduction. The finite-element gap tests share the nominal sections with the analytical model, and the omitted engagement-transition phases may carry information that cannot be counted until their contact is resolved. Profile-likelihood thresholds are nominal diagnostics because discrepancy is deterministic. Future work should (i) apply the support diagnostic to measured transmission error from gears with certified relief, (ii) resolve engagement transitions and fillet contact in the forward model, and (iii) replace the assumed noise scale and nominal likelihood thresholds by a calibrated discrepancy model within a Bayesian framework [40,41]. The finite stress controls in Section 4.8 relax the independent-noise and same-compliance assumptions under specified synthetic alternatives. They do not resolve the omitted FE transition stations or provide measured waveform calibration. Supplementary Table S27 maps each remaining evidence gap to a concrete follow-up experiment; these follow-ups have not been performed here.

changed_existing_paragraphs.before: The defensible outcome is an operator-conditioned account of observability and uncertainty, together with a pre-inversion support check. Physical reconstruction of the relief profile remains contingent on independent mechanical and experimental validation, which is the main direction for future work.
changed_existing_paragraphs.after: The finite stress controls extend the numerical evidence to correlated noise, a gain error and a change of compliance formulation, with all optimizer attempts and bound hits retained. At the deeper generating truth, the 5% gain error raises median scaled dedendum error from 0.0896 to 1.56, while the median observation residual is 0.138 µm. The defensible outcome remains an operator-conditioned account of observability and uncertainty, together with a pre-inversion support check. Physical reconstruction of the relief profile remains contingent on independent mechanical and experimental validation.
